t.1.202.1: Nārada said: As soon as the festival was over, the two of them, both coveting the three worlds, took counsel together, and then they gave orders to their army.
t.1.202.2: Given leave by their friends, by the elders of the Daityas and by their ministers, the two of them performed the rites for departure and then set out by night, under the constellation Maghā.
t.1.202.3: The two set out with a great army of Daityas, loyal and sharing their purpose, bearing maces and sharp-edged spears, with tridents and hammers in their hands.
t.1.202.5: Those two Daityas, both able to go wherever they wished and mad for battle, flew up into the sky and went to the very abode of the gods.
t.1.202.4: Praised by the Cāraṇas with auspicious blessings and with hymns bound up with victory, the two set out in the highest joy.
t.1.202.7: Those two of fierce valor, having conquered the world of Indra, then likewise vanquished the hosts of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and also the beings that move through the sky.
t.1.202.6: Learning of the coming of those two and of that boon granted by the Lord, the gods then abandoned Triviṣṭapa and went to the world of Brahmā.
t.1.202.8: Having conquered the Nāgas who dwell beneath the earth, those two great Asuras then vanquished all the Mleccha peoples who live by the sea.
t.1.202.9: Then the two of fierce command, having set out to conquer the whole earth, summoned their soldiers and spoke to them words that were very sharp.
t.1.202.10: The royal seers with great sacrifices, and the twice-born with offerings to the gods and to the ancestors, increase the splendor and the strength of the gods, and likewise their prosperity.
t.1.202.11: All these enemies of the Asuras, grown so mighty, must be slain by all of us acting together, with our whole strength.
t.1.202.12: Having thus instructed them all on the eastern shore of the great ocean, the two, set upon a cruel purpose, went forth in every direction.
t.1.202.13: Whatever twice-born men performed sacrifices, and those who officiated at sacrifices for others, all of them the two mighty ones slew by force as soon as they saw them.
t.1.202.14: In the hermitages of the seers of perfected selves, the soldiers of those two, emboldened and fearless, seized the sacred fires of the agnihotra and cast them into the waters.
t.1.202.16: When their curses did not take hold, like arrows loosed against rocks, the twice-born then abandoned their vows and fled.
t.1.202.15: Even the curses that the wrathful, great-souled ascetics rich in austerity pronounced did not take hold of those two, who swelled in might through the granting of the boon.
t.1.202.17: Those on earth who were perfected through austerity, self-controlled and devoted to tranquility, fled out of fear of those two, as serpents flee from Vainateya.
t.1.202.18: With its hermitages ravaged and shattered, their water-jars and sacrificial ladles scattered about, the whole world became empty, as if struck down by Time itself.
t.1.202.20: Taking the form of elephants in rut, their temples split and streaming, the two of them sent to Yama's abode even those who had hidden themselves in inaccessible places.
t.1.202.21: Becoming lions, then tigers, and then both becoming invisible, those two cruel ones, by these various means, slew the seers whenever they saw them.
t.1.202.19: As the royal seers and the seers kept themselves out of sight, the two great asuras, both bent on slaughter, made a firm resolve and began assuming various forms.
t.1.202.22: Then the earth became one where sacrifices and Vedic recitation had ceased, where kings and brahmins had perished, and where festivals and sacrificial rites had been abolished.
t.1.202.24: With farming and cattle-tending abandoned, its cities and hermitages destroyed, and strewn with bones and skeletons, the earth became terrible to behold.
t.1.202.23: Crying out in lamentation and stricken with fear, the earth saw its trade and markets come to a halt; the rites to the gods ceased, and it was bereft of auspicious marriages.
t.1.202.25: Then the world, with the rites for the ancestors abandoned and without the auspicious cry of vaṣaṭ, became terrible in appearance and hard to look upon.
t.1.202.26: The moon and the sun, the planets, the stars, the lunar mansions, and the dwellers of heaven fell into despair on seeing that deed of Sunda and Upasunda.
t.1.202.27: Thus the two Daityas, having conquered all the directions by cruel deeds, free of any rival, made their dwelling in Kurukṣetra.
